additional_reading.scope: Rechecked primary Results adaptive-timescale/conductance subsections, Discussion (including full spike trains), and Methods assessment of LN accuracy.
findings: A fixed transfer/filter at baseline can miss faster responses under large drive; the proposed adaptive-timescale extension still loses accuracy at very weak background noise. This is a limitation of the specified spiking-to-rate reduction, not a requirement to add an adaptive response to this application.
The comparison targets trial-averaged first-order firing-rate statistics; it does not validate full spike-train correlations or the closed-loop recurrent application.
Correlation can stay high while response scale or absolute error is material. The paper separately examines mean/variance and RMS distance; no numerical fidelity threshold is transferred.
additional_reading.limits: Image-rendered equations and numerical figure values were not independently decoded or measured. No author code, spiking simulation, neural training or reproduction. Current RateDynamics already states the relevant noise/reduction boundary; no new design mechanism or document change needed.
